property_summary: Only transactions sent from the contract's Owner address can cause c.withdraw() to reduce c's balance (i.e., non-Owner callers cannot make address(c).balance decrease via withdraw).
Only calls to withdraw made by C.Owner will NOT revert (i.e., withdraw reverts for non-Owner callers).
If the caller (tx.origin) is not the contract instance address (address(this)), then c.withdraw() must revert.
If the caller of the test is not the contract instance address, then calling c.withdraw() must revert.
If the caller of this test is not the contract instance, then calling c.withdraw() should revert.

For any caller and any calldata/value passed through Command to an arbitrary callee, the Owner remains able to withdraw the full contract balance only when withdraw is callable only by Owner; the mutant (which removes the withdraw require) allows anyone to trigger transfer to Owner causing withdraw semantics (caller's ability to move funds via withdraw) to differ — specifically, after invoking Command that forwards value to a callee that reverts, the correct contract still keeps balance withdrawable by Owner (i.e., address(c).balance unchanged by non-Owner), while the mutant can allow a non-Owner-triggered withdraw to have reduced balance.

For any caller and any calldata/value forwarded via Command, only the contract Owner can cause the contract balance to be sent out by withdraw; the mutant (which removes the Owner-only require in withdraw) allows a non-Owner caller to cause the contract balance to be transferred out (observable as address(c).balance becoming zero after such a call), violating this invariant for some inputs.

For any caller and any value, only the contract Owner can cause the contract's balance to leave via withdraw (so after a non-Owner calls Command forwarding value to any callee, the contract balance remains withdrawable by Owner); the mutant removing the Owner-only check in withdraw allows a non-Owner action to reduce address(c).balance (violating this invariant) for some inputs.

Invariant: Only the Owner can withdraw the contract balance, so after any sequence where a non-Owner calls Command forwarding value to an adversarial callee that reverts, the contract balance remains unchanged (Owner still owns the balance); the mutant (removing require in withdraw) allows anyone to trigger the transfer to Owner, letting a non-Owner-caused action make address(c).balance become zero for some inputs.

For every caller and value, only the Owner can cause the contract balance to be transferred out via withdraw; the mutant (which removes the Owner-only require in withdraw) allows a non-Owner to trigger a transfer that reduces address(c).balance, so there exists some caller/value sequence where address(c).balance becomes zero in the mutant but remains unchanged in the reference.

For any caller and any balance, calling withdraw transfers the entire contract balance to Owner (leaving contract balance 0); the mutant that transfers only half violates this because the contract balance remains >0 for some inputs.

For any caller and any starting contract balance, calling withdraw by the Owner empties the contract (address(c).balance == 0); the mutant that sends only half can leave a non-zero balance for some inputs.

If the owner calls withdraw when the contract has a strictly positive balance, the reference C always sends all funds out of the contract so address(c).balance == 0 afterwards; the mutant that sends only half will leave a non-zero balance for some positive balances, breaking this rule.

If the Owner calls withdraw when the contract has any non-zero balance, the reference transfers the entire contract balance to Owner so address(c).balance == 0 afterwards; the mutant that transfers only half can leave a positive balance, violating this.

For any owner caller and any incoming contract balance (including zero), when Owner calls withdraw the reference contract empties the contract (address(c).balance == 0); the mutant that transfers only half can leave a positive balance for some inputs, violating this property.

For any caller and any balance, after Owner (the deployer) calls withdraw(), the contract's balance becomes zero because the full balance is transferred to Owner; the mutant that transfers to msg.sender can leave the contract non-zero when Owner calls withdraw via a different msg.sender (i.e., when Owner is not the direct caller), so this rule is violated for some inputs.

For every caller X and any Ether balance, when Owner (the contract deployer) calls withdraw(), the contract's balance becomes zero afterwards (the reference always sends the full balance to Owner); the mutant sending to msg.sender can leave contract balance non-zero when Owner is not the immediate caller, so this property is violated for some inputs.
